_comment: Single source of truth for regional season windows, meaning when fruit ARRIVES in the US market (used by the supply panel). NOT in-country harvest dates — for grower-side phenology (harvest/flowering/sizing on the weather panel) see crop_calendar.json. Supply is now grouped by ORIGIN, so peru/colombia/chile/other are LIVE separately-tracked regions (no longer future placeholders); their windows are US arrival windows and must not be overwritten with in-country harvest dates. Dates are month-day (MM-DD); windows may wrap the new year. 'grace_weeks' = how many weeks past window edges data may still trickle in before a gap counts as unexpected. Edit this file at the March/September checkpoints — nothing else needs to change for a normal season transition.

regions.name: Mexico
regions.notes: Year-round. A gap here is ALWAYS unexpected — investigate immediately.

regions.name: California (South District)
regions.notes: CA harvest typically spring through late summer. USDA reporting often trails the field by a couple weeks on both ends — hence the grace window.

regions.name: Peru imports
regions.notes: Live separately-tracked region. Peru ships to the US roughly late spring through early fall.

regions.name: Colombia imports
regions.notes: Live separately-tracked region. Colombia ships in multiple flushes with variable timing; treated year-round with a wide grace window rather than hard edges.

regions.name: Chile imports
regions.notes: PROVISIONAL window. Chilean Hass arrives counter-season (roughly Oct through Feb, concentrated around Dec-Jan); dates inferred from history, not a published schedule. Widen if arrivals appear outside it.

regions.name: Other imports (mainly Dominican Republic)
regions.notes: Aggregate of everything not separately tracked — Dominican Republic (the bulk), Florida, Jamaica, Grenada, New Zealand. Some origin is almost always shipping, so year-round with grace since the mix shifts.
